title: Argument that Google's Fuchsia team is wasteful
why: Cost argument about retaining idle engineers; mostly opinion and assumption, with little concrete technical or business insight.

title: Apple quarterly results summarized against estimates
why: Quick earnings recap and market speculation; numbers are time-bound and it teaches no lasting lesson.

title: WP Engine co-founder responds to customer complaint
why: Company apology and damage control about one customer's outage; situational, not instructive for a general reader.

title: Why HN's comment markup rewrite was hard
why: HN's presentation was tangled with server logic, and scrapers depended on table markup, so changing markup risked breaking many apps.

title: Why scooter companies lack defensible moats
why: Network effects are local and cheap to break, since blanketing a city costs under $1.5M, so brand and durability matter more.

title: Opinion that consciousness is a useful illusion
why: Personal views and a critique of philosophy, backed by drug anecdotes rather than substantive argument or evidence.

title: Suspicion that a free-speech site is an agenda outlet
why: Political accusation about a news site's authors and funding; it argues a point but teaches no general lesson.

title: Musing that Chromium should be treated like Linux
why: Opinion on browser competition and privacy concerns without substantive technical explanation or evidence.

title: Personal experience of Facebook burying posts
why: Anecdote about personal posts getting less reach; a complaint about the platform rather than a transferable insight.

title: Argument against tech students' side hustles
why: Career advice based on mentoring anecdotes and opinion; persuasive but not a technical or informational lesson.

title: Teach problems before giving the solutions
why: People retain answers better after grappling with the problem; a git tutorial built around real pitfalls like detached HEAD illustrates it.

title: Argument against a secret list of felon officers
why: Political argument about felony records and rehabilitation, driven by personal grievance rather than informative explanation.

title: Pet theory that products have a peak version
why: Speculative theory about feature bloat and business incentives, offered without evidence or concrete mechanisms beyond opinion.

title: Romantic essay on the SR-71 Blackbird
why: Aesthetic appreciation of the SR-71 with unsourced claims about its development; evocative but not an explanation.

title: Early covid exponential-growth extrapolation
why: Speculative 2020 prediction from a non-expert; the edit notes logistic curves, but the core claim is an unverified forecast.

title: Defense of crypto via Star Trek fandom analogy
why: Opinion piece using a fandom analogy to argue crypto's merits; persuasive framing with no concrete technical substance.

title: Walking one-on-ones with voice-only calls
why: Personal work-habit report; voice-only technical talks may help, but it is a single experience rather than a tested guide.

title: Scandal shifted one commenter's moral outlook
why: Personal moral reflection after the VW scandal, centered on feelings about corruption rather than informative content.

title: List of profitable small web products
why: A self-promotional list of the commenter's own apps and build times, with no transferable method or analysis.

title: Sturgeon's law applied to biomedical research
why: Quoted interview opinion that most research is poor; a provocative claim without data or a method a reader can use.

title: Telegram's chats aren't end-to-end encrypted
why: Only Telegram's secret chats are end-to-end encrypted; regular cloud chats use server-held keys, so Telegram could read them.

title: Who pays determines how carefully money is spent
why: Four spending quadrants show that when someone else pays, people choose costly options less carefully, which helps explain rising tuition under aid.

title: Prediction that EVs will dominate and Tesla must adapt
why: Forward-looking market prediction and business advice about battery costs; plausible but speculative, not an established explanation.

title: Former Microsoft employee argues for breakup
why: Political and ethical argument for breaking up big tech firms, with personal reflection instead of verifiable analysis.

title: Frustration with a multi-round hiring process
why: Personal account of a drawn-out interview loop and a question about withdrawing; situational, with no general lesson.

title: Complaint about Apple's developer fee and open source
why: Opinion on Apple gatekeeping and developer costs; it does not explain how the system actually works.

title: Financial security reduces anxiety at work
why: Personal reflection on how financial security changes job happiness; relatable, but a single anecdote without a transferable method.

title: React Native skips the DOM for native performance
why: A React team member explains that React Native renders native views with no DOM, and that good mobile UX still requires deliberate performance work.

title: Why pipe benchmarks mislead without flushing
why: Python buffers stdout into 8KiB writes, so its pipe speed looked high until flush=True; benchmarks must control for buffering.

title: Doubt about rapid test effectiveness for Omicron
why: Personal experience of negative tests and a question about mass testing; anecdotal, without data or explanation.

title: Investors call bitcoin rat poison and a scam
why: Opinion citing famous investors and a personal prediction; assertions of worthlessness without a technical explanation.

title: Satirical phonetic spelling reform essay
why: Quoted satirical or humorous text about English spelling reform; entertaining but not an informative explanation.

title: Protest over Turkish government policies
why: Political commentary on the Istanbul protests and Turkish governance; opinion-driven and contextual to one event.

title: Free software lost the war despite winning battles
why: Opinion history of DRM and Linux adoption; reasonable framing, but mostly polemic with no concrete explanation.

title: Suspicion that ESA shifted Philae mission targets
why: Speculative accusation of spin based on edited FAQs and tweets; it asks questions but does not establish the facts.

title: Why classroom tech procurement is so hard
why: Schools must satisfy legal compliance, simplicity, price limits, long lifespans and layered bureaucracy simultaneously, which explains why vendors struggle.

title: Argument that intellectual property can't be stolen
why: Philosophical argument about copyright and proposed crowdfunded models; a stance and ideas, not an established explanation.

title: Commenter critiques the sociopath label for soldiers
why: Moral and political commentary on the military and the draft; opinion-based discussion with no technical or informative core.

title: Wishlist for a sharded, SQL-friendly database
why: Feature wishes for a database, framed as personal demands; it describes wants rather than explaining how systems work.

title: Critique of Assange's claims about Google
why: Argument about cryptography and Google's role, reacting to a book; persuasive debate with no new explanatory insight.

title: Dart team defends its open-source future
why: A team member replies to a troll about Dart's continuity; it reasserts that the compilers are open source, with little lasting teaching value.

title: Stock option taxes: NQOs, ISOs and 83(b)
why: NQOs tax the spread as income at exercise, ISOs can trigger AMT, and early exercise with an 83(b) election can defer tax on restricted stock.

title: Personal view that TypeScript slows developers
why: Opinion from someone trained on loosely typed languages; personal preference rather than evidence or a technical explanation.

title: Learning Perl made one programmer productive
why: Personal career story praising Perl's productivity; enthusiastic and anecdotal, without a concrete method a reader can apply.

title: Defense of systemd's integration goals
why: Argument for systemd and against Unix tradition; reasoned opinion, but it is a debate position rather than a technical explanation.

title: Statistics on racial disparities in policing
why: Political argument citing policing statistics and history; contested framing and advocacy rather than neutral explanation.

title: Python's built-in exception hierarchy
why: Lays out the full tree of built-in exceptions under BaseException, showing which categories to catch and how they nest.

title: Standard math path from algebra to measure theory
why: Outlines the usual sequence from high school algebra and geometry through linear algebra, ODEs, topology and measure theory, with computing relevance.

title: What contracting really costs beyond the rate
why: Contractors earn more because they absorb unpaid networking, admin, taxes and downtime that salaried employers otherwise subsidize.

title: Go far outruns Node.js in an HTTP benchmark
why: On 10,000 requests, single-process Node took 46s, clustered Node 17s and Go 3.5s, with full ab output showing the method.

title: Personal story of ADHD, addiction and medication
why: Deeply personal account of addiction and diagnosis; moving to read, but it carries no general lesson for technical readers.

title: Airbnb as a platform compared to YouTube
why: Legal and ethical opinion on platform liability; contextual argument about one case rather than a broadly useful explanation.

title: Critique of traditional universities and degrees
why: Polemic against universities and student loans, built on personal grievance and political framing rather than evidence.

title: Defense of NSA employees against public criticism
why: Emotional reply defending NSA staff's sacrifices; heated opinion rather than an informative account of how the agency works.

title: Why an entrepreneur left the US for Europe
why: Personal relocation reasons such as cost of living and politics; a life-choice account with no transferable lesson.

title: Post-Snowden privacy threatens internet history
why: Argument that privacy norms may erase early online culture; a thoughtful stance, but mostly opinion without concrete method.

title: Skip basic questions when code samples already exist
why: Hiring opinion that interviews should verify submitted work and fit; reasonable advice, but mostly a personal preference.

title: Why trivial requests have hidden design costs
why: Argument about the Elm package dispute that stays general; it makes a point about hidden consequences but teaches no specific technique.

title: Adderall revealed an undiagnosed ADHD focus effect
why: Personal diagnosis story and experience with stimulants; relatable, but a single anecdote and not an informative guide.

title: Relative's account of traveling homelessness
why: Anecdote about a relative's seasonal homeless lifestyle and free transit; vivid but one biased account, not a general lesson.

title: Reading football formations from TV footage
why: Count tight ends and backfield alignment to infer run versus pass; defenders' positions can be inferred from the offensive setup.

title: Why private information should stay private
why: Argument that privacy is a personal right, illustrated with hypothetical harms; a persuasive stance rather than substantive explanation.

title: Debate over measuring programmers under pressure
why: Disagreement about whether nervous-pressure interviews reveal skill; opinion and experience with no decisive evidence.

title: Why hits can't be predicted in music
why: Hits are usually surprises, and disrupting labels means understanding points, mechanical royalties and publishing, which the labels rely on.

title: Engineers aren't proximately responsible for misuse
why: Ethical argument that inventors are not proximate causes of misuse; a philosophical position without new technical content.

title: Why blockchain can't settle contested land ownership
why: A blockchain only records what it is given; bribery, conflicting claims and court rulings still need institutions, so the ledger solves none of it.

title: Abolishing copyright and film production economics
why: Thought experiment about the studio model without copyright; a plausible argument, but speculative and opinion-driven.

title: Flame war over a floating-point critique
why: Argumentative exchange about plagiarism and a critique's tone; personal and heated, with no clear teaching payload.

title: Why cumulative diffs speed up apt updates
why: Debian does not generate cumulative diffs, forcing clients to fetch many small patches; at Cydia scale this makes a large speedup worth it.

title: Rebuttal that Mandarin unity is unnatural
why: Heated rebuttal about Chinese and Romance language variation and Hong Kong politics; opinion with contested claims.

title: Low returns hurt retirement more than mortgages help
why: Lower expected investment returns raise the savings needed for retirement, often outweighing the benefit of cheap mortgage financing for a buyer.

title: The four group axioms explained with addition
why: A group needs identity, inverses, associativity and closure; abelian groups also commute, illustrated with addition and matrix examples.

title: Stakes of reopening the ConnectU case
why: Legal analysis of exposure in a news event; detailed, but tied to a specific dispute with no lasting technical lesson.

title: Deep nets as learned compact representations
why: Deep layers turn raw pixels into compact, task-specific features like edges and curves, discarding redundancy the classifier does not need.

title: Three routes into algorithmic trading
why: Break in through MIT-style hiring, join a prop shop and build tooling, or join a trading firm technically and move up; each route has trade-offs.

title: Critique of introversion as a fixed identity
why: Personal view that introvert identity can excuse avoiding things; a persuasive opinion, without research or a method.

title: Profiting from scarce buffs in Star Wars Galaxies
why: Entertaining account of exploiting a timed resource in a game; a fun anecdote with limited general lesson.

title: Personal account of police treatment in France
why: Personal experience and political commentary on policing in the suburbs; situational and opinion-based.

title: Management as clearing a path through dung
why: Maze analogy argues that coordination work clears the way for engineers' output, so managers are not pure cost even if they write no code.

title: Boston bombing exposes NSA surveillance limits
why: Sarcastic critique of NSA bulk data and the Boston bombing; political opinion with no concrete technical explanation.

title: General advice on improving English writing
why: Encouragement and a book recommendation; the substantive phonology point is cut short, leaving mostly general advice.

title: Rebuttal of a video's claims on policing
why: Political argument against a commentator's statistics and video; contested framing rather than neutral explanation.

title: A passenger's account of air traffic control on 9/11
why: Vivid first-hand passenger story of radio traffic; compelling, but a passenger's impression rather than expert explanation.

title: Scottish independence argument against the Union
why: Political argument for Scottish independence, dismissing critics and opponents; advocacy rather than informative content.

title: Go's toolchain descends from Plan 9
why: Go's compiler and linker inherit Plan 9's special C dialect and toolchain, which explains the self-contained build and its bootstrap history.

title: Personal n=1 report on inflammation and mood
why: Single-person anecdote linking diet and infection to mental health; no controls or evidence, so it cannot support a general claim.

title: Why voluntary online polls can't describe populations
why: Self-selected responses are not a random sample, so HN poll results cannot infer the community's geographic or age distribution.

title: Why the shopping cart patent was invalidated
why: The Federal Circuit ruled on obviousness on its own initiative, despite a jury verdict and earlier patent re-exam approvals.

title: Why Turing machines model all computation
why: A finite brain and finite paper have finitely many distinguishable states, so any mathematician's procedure reduces to a table of transitions.

title: Debate over patents protecting a tremor spoon
why: Argument about patents and competition, reacting to a company's product; opinion-led, with little technical explanation.

title: DEC's Alpha and Intel's Pentium-era dispute
why: Insider history of DEC shopping Alpha as a second source and of an Intel lawsuit; contested claims from one commenter, so treat as partial.

title: Why most Uber-for-X services fail on LTV
why: Infrequent services make customer acquisition costs exceed lifetime value, unlike Uber's frequent rides or Geico's retention-heavy model.

title: Observatory worker on the TMT protests
why: First-hand account of protests and state response at Mauna Kea; a political and local story with no general technical lesson.

title: SAFe borrows heavily from Reinertsen's flow principles
why: A SAFe-certified practitioner says SAFe is about 80% based on Reinertsen's book, so reading the source is more useful than rigid training.

title: Frustration with venture capital deal terms
why: Opinion and negotiating anecdotes about double dipping; there are concrete complaints, but mostly grievance rather than a clear guide.

title: Reproduced deleted post on a hosting suspension
why: Quoted hosting-company post about a PayPal dispute and account suspensions; a company controversy with limited general lesson.

title: Critique of Paul Graham on young CEOs
why: Argument that leadership and legal competence are not commodities and that VC age bias is harmful; opinion-based critique.

title: Personal taste ratings of Michelin restaurants
why: Subjective food ratings and a personal anecdote about dining; enjoyable, but taste opinions without an informative lesson.

title: Frustration with npm and modern front-end tooling
why: Opinion on npm installs and front-end complexity, from a returning developer's perspective; relatable critique without a clear fix.

title: Teach Gaussian elimination before vector spaces
why: Starting with linear systems motivates vector spaces, since many proofs reduce to row-reducing a matrix; the textbook order should follow that dependency.
